newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Hong Kong boss says British keep him out.
newsitem.headline: China's Hong Kong boss says British keep him out.

text.p: China's Hong Kong policy chief on Tuesday accused British authorities of blocking his entry into the colony by withholding a renewal of his visa, Hong Kong's ATV television station reported from Beijing.

"They won't even give me a visa, how can I meet him?" Lu Ping said in an interview when asked if he would ever meet Hong Kong's British colonial governor Chris Patten before the territory reverts to China at midnight next June 30.
Lu said he had received a visa to enter Hong Kong from China which was valid until December 15 and had been unable to come to the British territory since then.
Sino-British relations have suffered jolts over Hong Kong's handover but this was the first accusation about visa problems levelled against the colonial authorities by China.
Lu said the problem was one reason a meeting of a committee that elected Hong Kong's post-colonial legislature was in China on December 21 instead of in Hong Kong.

"You go to Hong Kong to hold an election, but the British don't agree ... and refuse to cooperate. Why did they give this visa only until December 15? Obviously because of that. Because on December 21 the provisional legislature was being elected. So they would not allow me to go Hong Kong, would they?"
